action.en: something done to deal with a problem
action.ex: The council promised quick action on the broken streetlights.

adjustment.ex: We made a small adjustment to the timetable.

administrative.en: about running an organisation or its paperwork
administrative.ex: The school hired extra staff for administrative tasks.

advised.en: told someone what they should do
advised.ex: The doctor advised him to rest for a week.

advising.en: telling someone what they should do
advising.ex: Experts are advising people to save more money.

again.ex: The shop opened again after the repairs.

agreed.en: decided together to make a deal
agreed.ex: The two sides agreed a new contract on Friday.

aim.ex: The aim of the course is to improve speaking skills.

allows.ex: The park allows dogs on a lead.

annually.ex: The festival is held annually in August.

applies.en: is used or has effect for something
applies.ex: This rule applies to all new students.

approval.en: official agreement that something can happen
approval.ex: The plan needs approval from the city council.

approve.ex: The board will approve the budget next week.

approved.ex: The new park was approved by local leaders.

at.en: used to show a point or level

back.ex: After the holiday, the prices were back to normal.

big.ex: They live in a big house near the sea.

billed.en: described publicly in a certain way
billed.ex: The match was billed as the game of the year.

blunder.ex: Sending the email to everyone was a big blunder.

bought.ex: She bought a new bike last week.

bring.ex: The city will bring in new bus routes next year.

burden.en: a heavy duty or cost that is hard to bear
burden.ex: High rent is a heavy burden for young workers.

example.en: The new rules will ease the burden on small firms.
example.zh: 新規定將減輕小企業的負擔。

note.meaning: 負擔；沉重的責任或成本。
note.usage: 常見 administrative/financial burden；place a burden on sb；ease the burden。

noteEn.meaning: a heavy duty or cost that is hard to deal with.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las nuevas normas aliviarán la carga de las pequeñas empresas.
noteEs.usage: Se usa administrative/financial burden; a burden on someone.

noteHi.exampleTr: नए नियम छोटी कंपनियों का बोझ कम करेंगे।
noteHi.usage: administrative/financial burden; a burden on sb आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい規則は中小企業の負担を軽くする。
noteJa.usage: administrative/financial burden、a burden on 人 の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 규정은 소기업의 부담을 덜어 줄 것이다.
noteKo.usage: administrative/financial burden, a burden on 사람 형태가 흔하다.

business.ex: Small business owners met the mayor on Monday.

businesses.en: companies that make or sell things
businesses.ex: Many local businesses closed early during the storm.

but.en: used to add a contrasting idea

called.ex: Their new baby is called Rose.

came.ex: The problem came to light after a customer complained.

ccpc.en: Ireland's competition and consumer protection body
ccpc.ja: CCPC（競争・消費者保護委員会）
ccpc.zh: 競爭與消費者保護委員會（CCPC）

change.en: a time when something is made different
change.ex: There was a change to the train times today.

check.en: look at something to make sure it is right
check.ex: Please check your answers before you finish.

checked.en: looked at carefully to make sure it is right
checked.ex: All bags are checked at the airport.

checks.en: careful looks to make sure things are right
checks.ex: The factory has safety checks every month.

clearance.en: official permission for something to happen
clearance.ex: The plane waited for clearance to take off.

combined.ex: Their combined income is enough to buy a house.

come.ex: Spring will come early this year.

commission.en: an official group with a special job
commission.ex: A commission was set up to study the problem.

committed.ex: The company has committed to cutting its waste.

companies.en: businesses that make or sell things
companies.ex: Two tech companies opened offices in the city.

competition.ex: Strong competition keeps prices low for buyers.

completed.ex: She completed the course in six months.

concluded.ex: The two countries concluded a trade agreement.

consequence.ex: Losing his job was a consequence of being late.

consequently.ex: It rained all day; consequently, the match was cancelled.

example.en: He missed the bus and consequently arrived late.
example.zh: 他錯過了公車，因此遲到了。

note.usage: 連接副詞，多放句首並加逗號，用於正式寫作表示因果。

noteEn.usage: Often at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma.

noteEs.exampleTr: Perdió el autobús y, en consecuencia, llegó tarde.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir al inicio de la frase con coma; registro formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: उसकी बस छूट गई और परिणामस्वरूप वह देर से पहुँचा।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक लेखन में वाक्य की शुरुआत में अल्पविराम के साथ।

noteJa.exampleTr: 彼はバスに乗り遅れ、その結果遅刻した。
noteJa.usage: 文頭でコンマとともに使うことが多い。フォーマルな書き言葉。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그는 버스를 놓쳐서 결과적으로 늦게 도착했다.
noteKo.usage: 주로 문장 앞에 쉼표와 함께 쓰며 격식 있는 글에 쓴다.

consumer.en: a person who buys things or services
consumer.ex: Consumer rights protect people who buy faulty goods.

contingent.ex: The job offer is contingent on a health check.

example.en: Our trip is contingent on the weather.
example.zh: 我們的旅行要看天氣而定。

note.usage: 固定搭配 contingent on/upon sth，多用於正式文體，相當於 depending on。

noteEn.usage: Use 'contingent on/upon'; it is a formal word.

noteEs.usage: Se usa contingent on/upon; es formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: हमारी यात्रा मौसम पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.usage: contingent on/upon sth = किसी चीज़ पर निर्भर; औपचारिक शब्द।

noteJa.exampleTr: 私たちの旅行は天気次第だ。
noteJa.meaning: 他のことに左右される；〜を条件とする。
noteJa.usage: contingent on/upon ～ の形で使う。硬い表現。

noteKo.meaning: 다른 것에 달려 있는; ~을 조건으로 하는.

cut.ex: The shop will cut prices next week.

date.ex: Please write the date at the top of the page.

deadline.en: the latest time something must be done
deadline.ex: The deadline for the essay is Friday.

deal.ex: The company signed a deal with a new supplier.

deals.en: business agreements, such as buying a company
deals.ex: The bank made several big deals this year.

department.en: a part of a government with a job
department.ex: She works in the health department.

determine.en: find out or decide something exactly
determine.ex: Tests will determine the cause of the fire.

drive.en: an organised effort to achieve something
drive.ex: The city began a drive to plant more trees.

duly.en: as expected or as was right
duly.ex: The letter duly arrived on Monday.
duly.ja: 予想どおり；当然のように

during.en: throughout or at a point in a time

earliest.ex: We will reply at the earliest possible time.

early.en: near the start of a time
early.ex: We arrived early to get good seats.

enforcement.en: making sure people obey a law
enforcement.ex: Stricter enforcement of speed limits saved lives.

example.en: The city promised stricter enforcement of parking rules.
example.zh: 市政府承諾更嚴格地執行停車規定。

note.meaning: 執行；強制實施（法律或規定）。
note.usage: 常見 law enforcement（執法）、enforcement action（執法行動）。

noteEn.meaning: making sure people obey a law or rule.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ciudad prometió aplicar con más rigor las normas de aparcamiento.
noteEs.meaning: hacer cumplir una ley o norma.
noteEs.usage: Combinaciones comunes: law enforcement, enforcement action.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर ने पार्किंग नियमों को सख़्ती से लागू करने का वादा किया।
noteHi.usage: law enforcement, enforcement action आम संयोजन हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 市は駐車規則の取り締まり強化を約束した。
noteJa.meaning: 法律や規則を執行すること。
noteJa.usage: law enforcement（法執行）、enforcement action（執行措置）がよく使われる。

noteKo.exampleTr: 시는 주차 규정을 더 엄격히 단속하겠다고 약속했다.
noteKo.usage: law enforcement(법 집행), enforcement action(집행 조치)이 흔하다.

enterprise.en: business; used in the ministry's name
enterprise.ex: The Minister for Enterprise spoke at the conference.

error.ex: There was an error in the bill.

establish.en: find out facts that prove something
establish.ex: Police are trying to establish what happened.

face.en: have to deal with something difficult
face.ex: Many farmers face a hard winter.

fair.ex: Everyone wants a fair price for their work.

finalised.ex: They finalised the wedding plans last night.

find.en: discover something is in a situation
find.ex: You may find the test easier than you think.

finished.ex: He finished his homework before dinner.

firms.ex: Many firms now let staff work from home.

fixed.en: set and not able to change
fixed.ex: The course has a fixed start date.

for.en: intended to help or be used by

former.ex: The former mayor still lives in the town.

found.ex: She found her keys under the sofa.

government.en: the group of people who run a country
government.ex: The government will build new hospitals.

government's.ex: The government's plan was popular with voters.

gun-jumping.en: completing a merger before official approval
gun-jumping.ex: Gun-jumping can bring large fines for companies.
gun-jumping.hi: गन-जंपिंग (मंज़ूरी से पहले सौदा पूरा करना)
gun-jumping.ja: ガンジャンピング（承認前の取引実行）
gun-jumping.zh: 搶跑（未獲批准即完成併購）

happen.ex: Accidents often happen near this corner.

houses.ex: Both houses of Congress passed the bill.

however.ex: The food was cheap; however, it was very good.

identified.ex: The problem was identified during testing.

implement.en: put a plan or rule into action
implement.ex: The school will implement the new rules in May.

increased.ex: The shop increased its prices in January.

intends.ex: She intends to study law next year.

internal.ex: The company held an internal meeting about pay.

introduce.ex: The town will introduce a new bus service.

investigation.en: an official careful study of facts
investigation.ex: Police started an investigation into the fire.

join.ex: The two clubs decided to join together.

joined.ex: The two schools joined to form one big school.

june.en: the sixth month of the year

lapsed.en: stopped being valid after time ran out
lapsed.ex: My library card lapsed last month.

example.en: He forgot to renew his insurance, so it lapsed.
example.zh: 他忘了續保，所以保險失效了。

note.meaning: （法令、合約等）因期限已過而失效。
note.usage: 不及物動詞：the order/licence lapsed；也可作名詞 a lapse（失誤）。

noteEn.meaning: to stop being valid because time has run out.
noteEn.usage: It has no object: 'The licence lapsed.'

noteEs.exampleTr: Olvidó renovar su seguro, así que caducó.
noteEs.meaning: dejar de ser válido al pasar el plazo.
noteEs.usage: Verbo intransitivo: the order lapsed (la orden caducó).

noteHi.exampleTr: वह बीमा नवीनीकृत करना भूल गया, इसलिए वह समाप्त हो गया।
noteHi.meaning: समय बीतने पर अमान्य हो जाना।
noteHi.usage: अकर्मक क्रिया: the order lapsed = आदेश समाप्त हो गया।

noteJa.exampleTr: 彼は保険の更新を忘れたので、失効してしまった。
noteJa.meaning: 期限切れで効力を失う。
noteJa.usage: 自動詞：the order lapsed（命令が失効した）。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그는 보험 갱신을 잊어서 보험이 만료되었다.
noteKo.usage: 자동사: the order lapsed(명령이 효력을 잃었다).

large.ex: A large crowd waited outside the stadium.

law.en: a rule made by a government
law.ex: The new law protects workers' rights.

legislation.ex: New legislation bans smoking in cars with children.

lifting.ex: The bank is lifting interest rates again.

light.ex: New facts came to light during the trial.

limit.en: the highest or lowest amount allowed
limit.ex: There is a limit of two bags per person.

limits.en: amounts that set when rules apply
limits.ex: The city set new limits on car noise.

lower.ex: Shops offer lower prices in the summer sales.

made.ex: The decision was made after a long meeting.

merger.en: when two companies join to become one
merger.ex: The merger created the largest bank in the country.

mergers.en: joinings of two companies into one
mergers.ex: Mergers often lead to job losses.

minister.en: a person who leads a government department
minister.ex: The minister visited the new school.

mistake.ex: I made a mistake in my phone number.

move.en: an action done to achieve something
move.ex: Cutting taxes was a popular move.

need.ex: You need a ticket to enter the museum.

never.ex: She has never been to Spain.

nevertheless.ex: The road was icy; nevertheless, we drove home safely.

new.ex: The library has a new computer room.

notification.ex: You will receive notification of your exam results by email.

notified.ex: All staff were notified of the change by email.

notify.ex: Please notify us if you change your address.

now.ex: The shop is now open on Sundays.

objective.ex: Our main objective is to reduce costs.

obliged.en: required by law or rule to do something
obliged.ex: Drivers are obliged to wear seat belts.

example.en: Shops are obliged to give refunds for faulty goods.
example.zh: 商店有義務為瑕疵商品退款。

note.meaning: （依法或依規定）有義務做某事。
note.usage: be obliged to do sth 表示「必須、有義務」；feel obliged to 表示「覺得不得不」。

noteEn.meaning: required by law or a rule to do something.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las tiendas están obligadas a reembolsar los productos defectuosos.
noteEs.meaning: obligado por ley o norma a hacer algo.
noteEs.usage: Se usa be obliged to + verbo.

noteHi.exampleTr: दुकानें खराब सामान पर पैसे लौटाने के लिए बाध्य हैं।
noteHi.meaning: कानून या नियम से कुछ करने के लिए बाध्य।
noteHi.usage: be obliged to do sth = कुछ करने के लिए बाध्य होना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 店は欠陥品に対して返金する義務がある。
noteJa.meaning: 法律や規則により〜する義務がある。
noteJa.usage: be obliged to do で「〜する義務がある」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 상점은 결함 있는 상품에 대해 환불해 줄 의무가 있다.
noteKo.usage: be obliged to do: ~할 의무가 있다.

obtained.ex: He obtained a visa to work abroad.

office.en: an official organisation that does a job
office.ex: The tax office sent me a letter.

oireachtas.ja: オイレクタス（アイルランド議会）

old.ex: We went back to the old timetable.

only.ex: The shop has only one cashier today.

opportunity.en: a time when something is possible
opportunity.ex: This job is a great opportunity for her.

order.en: an official legal instruction from a minister
order.ex: The court issued an order to close the factory.

orders.ex: Such orders must be published in the official paper.

oversight.en: a mistake caused by not noticing something
oversight.ex: Forgetting to sign the form was an oversight.

example.en: Your name was left off the list through an oversight.
example.zh: 由於疏忽，你的名字被漏列在名單上。

note.meaning: 疏忽；因沒注意而造成的錯誤。（另有「監督」之意）
note.usage: an oversight 指失誤；by/through an oversight 表示「由於疏忽」。

noteEn.meaning: a mistake made by not noticing something.

noteEs.exampleTr: Por un descuido, su nombre no aparecía en la lista.
noteEs.meaning: error por no fijarse en algo.
noteEs.usage: Se dice by/through an oversight (por descuido).

noteHi.exampleTr: चूक से आपका नाम सूची से छूट गया।
noteHi.meaning: ध्यान न देने से हुई चूक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 手違いであなたの名前がリストから漏れていた。
noteJa.meaning: 注意不足による見落とし・手落ち。
noteJa.usage: through an oversight で「うっかりミスで」。

paperwork.en: official forms and documents to complete
paperwork.ex: Buying a house involves a lot of paperwork.

parliament.en: the group that makes a country's laws
parliament.ex: Parliament will vote on the bill next week.

part.en: on the part of: made or done by
part.ex: The delay was a mistake on the part of the airline.
part.zh: on the part of：在…方面；由…造成

parts.en: sections of something, here of parliament

period.ex: Prices rose during the holiday period.

permits.ex: The ticket permits entry to all the museums.

plans.ex: She plans to visit Japan next spring.

possible.en: able to happen or be done
possible.ex: Please reply as soon as possible.

previous.ex: The previous owner painted the house blue.

prices.ex: Food prices went up again this month.

prior.ex: Please arrive ten minutes prior to the start.

promised.en: said you will surely do something
promised.ex: He promised to call me tonight.

protection.ex: Sun cream gives protection against burns.

punish.en: make someone suffer for doing wrong
punish.ex: The school will punish students who cheat.

pursue.ex: The police will pursue the case in court.

raised.ex: The café raised the price of coffee.

raising.ex: The club is raising its fees next year.

recent.ex: Recent rain has filled the rivers.

red.en: red tape: too many official rules and forms
red.ex: Red tape slows down new building projects.

reducing.ex: We are reducing plastic in our shop.

refraining.ex: Please refrain from talking during the film.

example.en: Passengers are asked to refrain from smoking.

note.usage: 固定用法 refrain from doing sth，語氣正式，常見於公告或官方聲明。

noteEn.meaning: to choose not to do something.

noteEs.exampleTr: Se pide a los pasajeros que se abstengan de fumar.
noteEs.usage: Se usa refrain from + -ing; es formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: यात्रियों से धूम्रपान न करने का अनुरोध है।
noteHi.meaning: कुछ करने से खुद को रोकना।
noteHi.usage: refrain from doing sth = कुछ करने से परहेज़ करना; औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 乗客の皆様は喫煙をご遠慮ください。
noteJa.usage: refrain from doing の形。掲示や公式発表で多い硬い表現。

noteKo.exampleTr: 승객 여러분은 흡연을 삼가 주시기 바랍니다.
noteKo.usage: refrain from doing 형태로 쓰며 공지나 공식 발표에 자주 쓴다.

regulator.en: an official body that controls an industry
regulator.ex: The energy regulator capped gas prices.

report.en: officially tell an authority about something
report.ex: Please report any problems to the manager.

reported.ex: The theft was reported to the police.

reporting.en: officially telling an authority about something
reporting.ex: Reporting rules for small firms are simpler.

required.ex: A passport is required to travel abroad.

requirement.en: something that a rule says you must have
requirement.ex: A degree is a requirement for this job.

result.en: as a result: because of this
result.ex: As a result of the storm, schools closed.

review.ex: The company carried out a review of its costs.

revised.ex: The revised timetable starts next week.

revived.ex: The old festival was revived after twenty years.

said.ex: She said the shop was closed.

sales.en: the money a company gets from selling
sales.ex: The company's sales rose by ten percent.

says.ex: The teacher says the test is on Monday.

scrutiny.ex: The new plan is under close scrutiny.

example.en: The company's accounts came under close scrutiny.
example.zh: 這家公司的帳目受到嚴格審查。

note.usage: 常見 under scrutiny（受到審查）、come under scrutiny、close scrutiny。為不可數名詞。

noteEn.usage: Often 'under scrutiny' or 'come under scrutiny'; uncountable.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las cuentas de la empresa fueron sometidas a un examen minucioso.
noteEs.usage: Se usa under scrutiny o come under scrutiny; es incontable.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी के खातों की बारीकी से जाँच हुई।
noteHi.usage: under scrutiny = जाँच के दायरे में; अगणनीय संज्ञा।

noteJa.exampleTr: その会社の会計は厳しい精査を受けた。
noteJa.meaning: 細かく綿密に調べること。
noteJa.usage: under scrutiny（精査を受けて）、come under scrutiny の形が多い。不可算名詞。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 회사의 회계는 면밀한 조사를 받았다.
noteKo.usage: under scrutiny(조사를 받는), come under scrutiny 형태로 자주 쓴다. 불가산 명사.

secured.ex: The team secured a place in the final.

september.en: the ninth month of the year

set.ex: They set a date for the next meeting.

shoppers.en: people who buy things in shops
shoppers.ex: The shops were full of shoppers on Saturday.

signed.en: wrote his name on an official paper
signed.ex: The president signed the new law.

single.ex: He did not make a single mistake.

size.ex: The size of the company has doubled.

slash.ex: The store slashed prices by half.

so-called.ex: The so-called experts gave very poor advice.

specified.ex: Return the form within the specified time.

state.ex: She works in a state hospital.

statutory.ex: Workers have a statutory right to paid holidays.

example.en: Employers must pay the statutory minimum wage.
example.zh: 雇主必須支付法定最低工資。

note.usage: 放在名詞前：statutory deadline/right/duty，強調「法律要求的」。

noteEn.usage: Use before a noun: 'statutory deadline', 'statutory right'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los empleadores deben pagar el salario mínimo legal.
noteEs.meaning: establecido o exigido por la ley.
noteEs.usage: Va antes del sustantivo: statutory deadline/right/duty.

noteHi.exampleTr: नियोक्ताओं को वैधानिक न्यूनतम वेतन देना होगा।

noteJa.exampleTr: 雇用主は法定最低賃金を支払わなければならない。

stay.ex: Try to stay calm during the exam.

struck.ex: The two firms struck a deal last week.

subject.en: subject to: likely to receive or face
subject.ex: All bags are subject to search.

substantially.ex: Prices have risen substantially this year.

take.ex: The school will take steps to stop bullying.

tape.en: red tape: too many official rules
tape.ex: Cutting red tape helps small businesses grow.

tell.ex: Please tell the teacher if you are ill.

then.ex: We met in 2010; I was a student then.

threshold.en: the level at which a rule starts to apply
threshold.ex: Your income is below the tax threshold.

example.en: Families below the income threshold get free school meals.
example.zh: 收入低於門檻的家庭可獲免費學校午餐。

note.meaning: 門檻；某規定開始適用的數量或程度界線。
note.usage: 常用 threshold for/of sth；above/below the threshold 表示高於／低於門檻。

noteEn.meaning: the level at which a rule or effect starts.
noteEn.usage: Say 'above/below the threshold' or 'the threshold for something'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las familias por debajo del umbral de ingresos reciben comidas escolares gratis.

paragraphs: The Government made a mistake. Because of it, some recent business deals may now be checked.
When two companies join together, this is called a merger. Big mergers must be reported to a state office, the CCPC. It checks that prices stay fair for shoppers.
In June, the minister Peter Burke signed an order. It raised the limit for reporting from €60 million to €100 million in sales. He wanted less paperwork for companies.
But the parliament did not approve the order in time. So it stopped on 30 September. Now the old limit of €60 million is back.
The CCPC says companies should check their deals. It will not punish them because of this mistake. A new limit will come in 2027.
Some companies that joined together or bought other companies in recent weeks may now have their deals checked by the competition regulator. This is because of a mistake by the Government.

In June, the Minister for Enterprise, Peter Burke, signed an order about mergers. Companies must tell the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (CCPC) about large deals. The order raised the limit for this from €60 million in combined sales to €100 million. The minister wanted to reduce paperwork for businesses.

But orders like this need the approval of both parts of the Oireachtas, Ireland's parliament, within a fixed time. This did not happen, so the order stopped working on 30 September. The department found the mistake during a review.

Now the old, lower limit is back for deals made since then. The CCPC says companies should check if they need to report their deals. It has promised not to punish firms that finished deals without approval during this time.
The department plans to set new limits early in 2027. The law allows only one change each year.
Companies that agreed or completed mergers in recent weeks may face investigation by the competition regulator because of a mistake by the Government.

In June, the Minister for Enterprise, Peter Burke, signed an order raising the size at which deals must be reported to the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (CCPC). The limit for the combined turnover of the companies rose from €60 million to €100 million. The aim was to cut red tape for business.

However, such orders must be approved by both houses of the Oireachtas within a set time. This did not happen, so the order lapsed on 30 September. The Department of Enterprise said the error was found during an internal review.

As a result, the old, lower limit applies again to deals made since then. The CCPC is advising firms to check whether their deals need to be reported. It has promised not to take action against companies that completed deals without approval during this period.
The department says it will bring in new limits as early as possible in 2027, as the law allows only one change each year.

Businesses that have agreed or finalised mergers in recent weeks could find their transactions under the scrutiny of the competition watchdog, owing to an administrative blunder on the Government's part.

In June, the Minister for Enterprise, Peter Burke, signed an order lifting the threshold at which deals must be notified to the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (CCPC), raising the combined turnover trigger from €60 million to €100 million. The move was billed as part of a drive to slash red tape.

Such orders, however, require the approval of both houses of the Oireachtas within a statutory deadline. That approval was never secured, and the order duly lapsed on 30 September, an oversight the department says came to light during an internal review.

Consequently, the former, lower threshold has been revived for transactions struck since that date. The CCPC is urging firms to establish whether they are obliged to notify it, while undertaking not to pursue so-called gun-jumping, where a deal is completed before clearance, during this window.
The department intends to introduce revised thresholds at the earliest opportunity in 2027, since the legislation permits only a single adjustment per year.
Companies that have agreed or completed mergers in recent weeks may be subject to investigation by the competition regulator as a consequence of an error on the part of the Government.

In June, the Minister for Enterprise, Peter Burke, signed an order that increased the threshold above which transactions must be notified to the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (CCPC). The combined turnover requirement was raised from €60 million to €100 million, with the objective of substantially reducing the administrative burden on businesses.

Nevertheless, the validity of such orders is contingent upon approval by both houses of the Oireachtas within a specified period. Since this approval was not obtained, the order lapsed on 30 September. According to the department, the error was identified during an internal review.

Consequently, the previous, lower threshold now applies to transactions concluded since that date. The CCPC has advised firms to determine whether notification is required, and has committed to refraining from enforcement action against companies that completed deals prior to clearance during this period.
The department intends to implement revised thresholds as early as possible in 2027, given that the legislation permits only one adjustment annually.
